network_author.description: Build a rectangular grid network with `netgenerate`, no OpenStreetMap. Returns the source to put in the recipe and the built .net.xml artifact.

x_length.description: Length in metres of an x-direction edge. SUMO: 100.

x_number.description: Junctions along x, at least 2. SUMO: 5.

y_length.description: Length in metres of a y-direction edge. SUMO: 100.

y_number.description: Junctions along y, at least 2. SUMO: 5.

network_author.name: generate_grid

network_author.description: Build a spider-web network (arms crossed by concentric circles) with `netgenerate`, no OpenStreetMap. Returns the source to put in the recipe and the built .net.xml artifact.

arm_number.description: Number of arms, at least 3. SUMO: 13.

circle_number.description: Number of circles, at least 1. SUMO: 20.

omit_center.description: Leave out the central junction. SUMO: false.

space_radius.description: Distance in metres between circles. SUMO: 100.

network_author.name: generate_spider

network_author.description: Build a random network with `netgenerate`, no OpenStreetMap. The seed is required: the same seed and parameters give the same network. Returns the source to put in the recipe and the built .net.xml artifact.

iterations.description: Number of random growth steps, at least 1. SUMO: 200.

max_distance.description: Maximum distance in metres, at least min_distance. SUMO: 250.

min_distance.description: Minimum distance in metres between nodes. SUMO: 100.

seed.description: Seed of the generator, at least 0.

network_author.name: generate_random

network_import.description: List the import profiles `netconvert` can use (what the imported network keeps: roads, rail, bicycle lanes, pedestrian paths) and the vehicle classes `keep_vclass` accepts. Public transport stops and lines and polygons are not part of any profile.
network_import.name: list_import_profiles

network_import.description: Download the OpenStreetMap data of an area of interest, once per polygon (a second call for the same area reuses the stored snapshot). Name the area with exactly one of `bbox`, `polygon` or `place_name` (an administrative boundary, resolved to a polygon). Put any extra thing the user asked for in `requirements`, for example 'bus stops'. Returns the `source` and the `osm_snapshot` for the recipe, or `needs_user` when the area is above the size limit, the place is not a boundary, or a requirement is unsupported (public transport stops and lines); then nothing was downloaded.

place_name.description: Name of an administrative area, e.g. 'Sant Antoni'.

polygon.description: Closed ring of [lat, lon] points, at most about 200 vertices.

requirements.description: What else the user asked for, in their words, e.g. ['bus stops'].

network_import.name: fetch_osm

network_import.description: Build the network from a fetched snapshot with `netconvert`: the chosen import profile, cut to the area's polygon, keeping the largest connected component. Starts the cleanups again. Returns the `netconvert_options` and `net_artifact` for the recipe.
network_import.name: netconvert

network_import.description: Rebuild keeping only the largest connected component, so no piece of road is cut off from the rest. `netconvert` already does it; this makes the choice explicit after other cleanups. Returns the updated options.
network_import.name: keep_largest_component

network_import.description: Rebuild removing isolated edges (edges that connect to nothing at either end).
network_import.name: remove_isolated

network_import.description: Rebuild joining junctions that are close together (a big crossing mapped as several nodes) into one.
network_import.name: join_junctions

network_import.description: Rebuild keeping only the edges that allow a vehicle class, for example 'passenger' to drop rail and pedestrian-only paths.
network_import.name: keep_vclass
